A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoRefine and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Existing material can be matched reliably despite the added table and subsequent renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original AutoRefine benchmark results, component ablations, retrieval analyses, training dynamics, and case studies in Section 3 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds model-size and evaluation-metric comparisons in Section 3.4.2 and Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same trajectory generation, refinement prompt, rewards, and masked GRPO objective. The added 7B experiment applies the existing method at another model size without introducing a procedural or architectural component.

E1.justification: Training remains NQ plus HotpotQA, and evaluation retains the same seven QA datasets and static Wikipedia retrieval environment. Table 3's 'General QA' heading covers the existing NQ, TriviaQA, and PopQA datasets; it does not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding existing experiments. The added size/metric study reuses Search-R1 as its comparator. Newly cited related works are not added to the reported empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 3 substantially extends the previous 3B/EM evaluation design with Qwen2.5-7B-Base and F1/CEM scoring at both model sizes. Section 3.3.2 also changes the stated answer-action metric for Figure 5 from exact match to CEM; its unchanged curves do not establish that this analysis was rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 3.4.2 tests model-size sensitivity and whether AutoRefine's advantage persists across EM, F1, and CEM. These add substantive analytical questions beyond the retained component ablations, retrieval-depth tests, training dynamics, and case studies.

E5.justification: The added table follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice, without new seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing training curves and token-length distribution reporting are retained.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds 7B EM/F1/CEM results and 3B F1/CEM results across all seven benchmarks. At 7B, AutoRefine averages 0.455/0.536/0.486, versus Search-R1's 0.408/0.483/0.443, respectively. The 3B EM rows repeat the earlier results, so this is a substantial extension under additional conditions, not an improvement in unchanged 3B scores.

T1.justification: The task formulation, reward definitions, and GRPO objective in Equations 1–4 are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, derivations, or formal properties are added; the CEM discussion concerns empirical evaluation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: explicit knowledge refinement, retrieval-specific rewards, and improved QA performance. The new experiments supply supporting evidence without revising these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.4.2 newly interprets larger models as better able to exploit retrieval-augmented reasoning and F1/CEM as providing more nuanced evaluation. Existing limitations remain unchanged, including statements about exclusively 3B models and exact-match evaluation that now conflict with the added study.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions and Appendix B retain the same hardware, hyperparameters, rollout settings, data processing, and code/data access information. No separate implementation instructions accompany the new 7B results.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds citations to ManuSearch, s3, R1-Searcher++, and SEM. These modestly update related-work coverage while retaining the existing positioning around explicit refinement and retrieval-specific rewards.

P1.justification: v3 divides Section 3.4 into component and size/metric subsections, adds localized explanatory paragraphs, revises the action-metric wording, and corrects the author name Shihan Li to Sihang Li. The broader narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the model-by-metric Table 3 and changes Figure 5's caption from 'success rates' to 'recall'. Existing figure graphics are retained. Appendix tables are renumbered from 3–5 to 4–6, with accompanying pagination changes.

improvement.justification: Table 3 strengthens support for the retained claims by showing that AutoRefine's advantage over Search-R1 persists at 7B and under F1/CEM, partly addressing v1's stated scale and metric limitations. This provides a limited net improvement, tempered by unrevised Sections 4–5 that still describe exclusively 3B/EM experiments and present 7B evaluation as future work.
